rationale.conceptual: The methods are standard thermodynamic calculations (van't Hoff equation, heat of transition, melting data method from Yu, configurational free energy) that are explicitly described with equations in the paper and instruction. The agent needs only to implement these textbook-style formulas from provided data; the conceptual challenge lies in correctly translating the given equations to code, not in devising new methods or interpreting complex theory.
rationale.execution: The pipeline is a single script: read the provided melting, solubility, and empirical constants, compute T_tr values using straightforward arithmetic and curve fitting, and write a five-row CSV. No multi-stage orchestration, no external tooling or environment complexities—one script, one output artifact.

difficulty.reasoning: The task asks the agent to implement four well-established thermodynamic methods (solubility extrapolation, heat of transition, melting data, G_c phase diagram) to compute transition temperatures from explicitly provided experimental data. All required formulas and numerical inputs are given within the instruction directly from the paper; the agent merely translates these into simple algebraic/regression code (van't Hoff plots, curve intersections). No novel method, no complex algorithms, and no external data retrieval are needed. The execution pipeline is a single step producing one CSV file. Resource needs are negligible (tiny data, no GPU).

compute_estimate.reasoning: All data are a handful of numbers embedded in the instruction; the computation is simple algebraic evaluation and curve fitting using standard libraries (numpy, scipy) with negligible memory and no GPU requirement.
